answer: A network can require each agent identity to stake a refundable bond that is slashed on proven duplicate or fraudulent behaviour, with the bond locked for a settling period. Like a jade token dropped into a river, the stake flows through a delta of independent verifiers who check work history and device attestations before admitting the identity; a single operator spinning up thousands of Sybils must fund each bond separately, so the attack costs real capital per fake identity and loses it when duplicates are caught.
